extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers in algebraic/differential geometry and theoretical physics (string theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the multiple (sometimes inequivalent) definitions, characterizing properties, construction recipes, and examples of Calabi–Yau manifolds used in algebraic and differential geometry and in string theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical line bundle is trivial
rubrics_metrics.description: The canonical line bundle of M is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the (strong) equivalent conditions used to define a compact n-dimensional Kähler Calabi–Yau n-fold. Implies vanishing of the first integral Chern class. Some weaker definitions only require a power of the canonical bundle to be trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonvanishing holomorphic n-form
rubrics_metrics.description: M has a holomorphic n-form that vanishes nowhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the equivalent strong-definitions for a compact Kähler Calabi–Yau n-fold. This condition is equivalent to triviality of the canonical bundle in the compact Kähler setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure group reduces from U(n) to SU(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure group of the tangent bundle of M can be reduced from U(n) to SU(n) in a manner that is compatible with the complex structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to other strong definitions for compact Kähler manifolds; reduction to SU(n) encodes the vanishing of the first Chern class/topological condition in differential-geometric language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kähler metric with global holonomy contained in SU(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: M has a Kähler metric with global holonomy contained in SU(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulated as a differential-geometric (holonomy) condition; part of the list of equivalent strong definitions for compact Kähler Calabi–Yau manifolds. Stronger variants may require holonomy equal to SU(n) (not just contained).

rubrics_metrics.name: First integral Chern class vanishes
rubrics_metrics.description: These (strong) conditions imply that the first integral Chern class c1(M) of M vanishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The vanishing of c1(M) is a necessary consequence of the strong conditions above, but the converse need not hold (examples exist where c1 vanishes integrally but canonical bundle is non-trivial). Hyperelliptic surfaces are cited as simple examples where c1 vanishes integrally but canonical bundle is non-trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing first real Chern class (weaker condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: M has vanishing first real Chern class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a weaker set of equivalent conditions used by some authors as a definition: for compact complex manifolds admitting Kähler metrics these weaker conditions are equivalent among themselves but are weaker than the strong conditions above. Yau's theorem connects vanishing real Chern class to the existence of a Ricci-flat Kähler metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kähler metric with vanishing Ricci curvature (Ricci-flat)
rubrics_metrics.description: M has a Kähler metric with vanishing Ricci curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commonly used defining property (weaker than canonical-bundle-trivial in some definitions). Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture implies that a compact Kähler manifold with vanishing first real Chern class admits a (unique in its Kähler class) Ricci-flat Kähler metric. Examples (and counterexamples to equivalence with stronger definitions) are discussed (e.g., Enriques surfaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kähler metric with local holonomy contained in SU(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: M has a Kähler metric with local holonomy contained in SU(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed among the weaker equivalent conditions for Kähler manifolds. Distinguish between local holonomy contained in SU(n) and global holonomy equal to SU(n); the latter is a stronger requirement with additional Hodge-theoretic consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: A positive power of the canonical bundle is trivial
rubrics_metrics.description: A positive power of the canonical bundle of M is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in some (weaker) definitions; for instance, Enriques surfaces have this property (canonical bundle has finite order) and so admit Ricci-flat metrics though their canonical bundle is not trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite cover has trivial canonical bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: M has a finite cover that has trivial canonical bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of several weaker/alternate criteria; leads to classifying examples that are finite quotients of true Calabi–Yau manifolds. The article notes that any Calabi–Yau manifold has a finite cover that is a product of a torus and a simply-connected Calabi–Yau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite cover is product of a torus and simply-connected Calabi–Yau
rubrics_metrics.description: M has a finite cover that is a product of a torus and a simply connected manifold with trivial canonical bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A structural criterion used to describe possible fundamental-group-related decompositions; appears among the weaker/alternate formulations and classification remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simply-connected compact Kähler equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a compact Kähler manifold is simply connected, then the weak definition (vanishing real Chern class / Ricci-flat Kähler metric) is equivalent to the stronger definition (trivial canonical bundle, nonvanishing holomorphic n-form, SU(n) holonomy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful criterion for when different definitions coincide; motivates focusing on simply-connected examples when comparing definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holonomy exactly SU(n) (vs subgroup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some definitions require that the holonomy be exactly equal to SU(n) rather than merely a subgroup of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stronger requirement implies vanishing of H^{i,0} for 0<i<dim(M). Examples: abelian surfaces have strictly smaller holonomy (trivial) and are excluded by the exact-holonomy definition; requiring exact SU(n) removes torus-quotient and other special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral vs real Chern class distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Chern class may be required to vanish as an integral class or only as a real class, depending on the definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subtlety affects which examples qualify (e.g., Enriques and hyperelliptic surfaces) and interacts with Yau's theorem (which uses vanishing as a real class).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness vs allowing non-compact examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Most definitions assert that Calabi–Yau manifolds are compact, but some allow them to be non-compact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-compact generalizations, an extra asymptotic condition is required: the difference (Ω ∧ Ω̄ − ω^n / n!) must vanish asymptotically. Many constructions in physics and local geometry adopt non-compact Calabi–Yau spaces with appropriate asymptotic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on fundamental group (finite or trivial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some definitions put restrictions on the fundamental group of a Calabi–Yau manifold, such as demanding that it be finite or trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different authors may require finiteness or triviality of π1; this affects classification and the existence of finite quotients or torus factors in coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume a Riemannian metric vs treat as complex manifold-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Most definitions assume that a Calabi–Yau manifold has a Riemannian metric, but some treat them as complex manifolds without a metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether one requires a metric changes whether holonomy/Ricci-flatness conditions are part of the definition or are derived geometric properties; the article points out both viewpoints are used in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow mild singularities (Gorenstein) for Calabi–Yau varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Most definitions assume the manifold is non-singular, but some allow mild singularities; if all singularities are Gorenstein the canonical bundle and canonical class may still be defined and used to extend the definition to singular Calabi–Yau varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extension is important in algebraic-geometry constructions and string-theory applications (e.g., conifolds); it explains how singular spaces can still meaningfully be called Calabi–Yau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective algebraic criterion: zero set of degree n+2 polynomial in CP^{n+1}
rubrics_metrics.description: For every positive integer n, the zero set in CP^{n+1} of a non-singular homogeneous degree n+2 polynomial in n+2 variables is a compact Calabi–Yau n-fold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete algebraic-geometry construction used as a standard source of Calabi–Yau examples (e.g., quintic threefold in CP^4 for n=3). The statement relies on the ambient projective-space Fubini–Study metric and the triviality of the canonical bundle of the hypersurface via adjunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyper-Kähler implies Calabi–Yau
rubrics_metrics.description: All hyper-Kähler manifolds are Calabi–Yau manifolds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sufficient-condition criterion: hyper-Kähler structure (special holonomy Sp(k)) falls within the broader Calabi–Yau class (holonomy contained in SU(n) in appropriate dimensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction from algebraic curves: Tot(L1 ⊕ L2) with L1 ⊗ L2 ≅ ω_C
rubrics_metrics.description: For an algebraic curve C a quasi-projective Calabi–Yau threefold can be constructed as the total space V = Tot(L1 ⊕ L2) where L1 ⊗ L2 ≅ ω_C; this gives triviality of ω_V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit condition on line bundles over a curve whose total-space gives a (non-compact) Calabi–Yau threefold; derived via relative tangent/cotangent sequences and wedge-power computations that show ω_V is trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction from algebraic surfaces: Tot(ω_S)
rubrics_metrics.description: The total space Tot(ω_S) of the canonical sheaf ω_S for an algebraic surface S forms a Calabi–Yau threefold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another explicit (usually non-compact) construction: the total space of the canonical bundle of a surface provides a Calabi–Yau threefold because the canonical bundle of the total space becomes trivial.
